nbas.name: GE Vernova GridOS
nbas.positioning: GridOS operates the electrical grid. DRS coordinates the human, organizational and resource crisis around the disruption.
nbas.status: DECLARED from the operator's research; confirm against vendor documentation in the S16 program

nbas.name: Veoci (Vitals EM)
nbas.positioning: Veoci runs the hospital's incident. DRS coordinates the healthcare system, its leadership and the affected population as one transparent, authority-controlled response environment.

nbas.name: YUDU Sentinel
nbas.positioning: Sentinel tells the campus. DRS fulfils the campus's needs: who lacks heat, which building has capacity, who has blankets, who is qualified, who approved the relocation, who has been helped.

nbas.name: CrisisCommand.ai (partner, not a competitor)
nbas.positioning: CrisisCommand thinks and commands. DRS coordinates and allocates beneath it; eXeL listens; R-CORE preserves, replays and improves.

personas.principle: Public participants do not receive the same authority as operational leaders. The platform maintains a validated roster and a rank / authority structure. AI recommends and organizes; authorized humans retain command.

conops.revision: Plan v1 → Event → Change → Authority → Plan v2 — the user reads: what changed, why, who authorized it, what to do now
conops.resilienceHeritage: Project Resilience CONOPS 1–7 (SRC-2 p.5): real-time alerts · user reporting · alert dissemination · resource management (inventory + gap analysis) · volunteer coordination · public communication · preparedness information — DRS keeps all seven and adds verified authority, plan versioning, polling, replay and scenario planning.

architecture.owner: eXeL AI Polling (this repository: sessions → responses → 3/6/9 themes with 33/111/333-word summaries → living rankings; 33 languages; responsive phone / desktop)

chain: SYNC / OPERATIONAL TRUTH — who knew what · who authorized what · what changed · what moved · what happened
rcore.statement: Every crisis becomes evidence. Every replay improves readiness. Every cycle strengthens resilience.
rcore.law: R-CORE is not the crisis application; it is the recursive operational architecture beneath it. No commit without a named human-authority event (MODE_R-CORE_SPEC).

nose.needs: Restore electricity / operations quickly while understanding impact, available backup capacity, community and facility needs, and who is responsible.
outcomes: Every need outside the grid (a facility without power, a plant without water, a neighbourhood without heat) is recorded, prioritized and assigned to a verified responder
Scarce backup capacity (generators, fuel, crews, shelters) is allocated against recorded needs, not requests by loudness
Every plan change carries who authorized it and why; the workforce and the public read the current plan
The event replays for the next one
nose.solution: DRS beside GridOS: GridOS restores the grid; DRS runs the verified roster, needs intake, resource allocation, plan versioning, polling and replay for the human and organizational crisis around it.

evidence.claim: Time from a recorded need to an assignment falls with DRS vs the pre-pilot baseline
evidence.experiment: Pilot one utility or plant through one simulated and one live disruption; log need → assignment → fulfilment timestamps (S16)

evidence.claim: Duplicate or misallocated resource deployments fall
evidence.experiment: Count duplicate assignments per event, baseline vs pilot

evidence.claim: Buyers pay for coordination outside the grid on top of GridOS
evidence.experiment: Outcome-based WTP interviews with three utility / industrial buyers (S14)

nose.needs: Give healthcare leaders, officials, clinicians and citizens enough trustworthy information to coordinate regional capacity without amplifying panic.
outcomes: A verified regional leadership / authority map
Demand-to-resource coordination across organizations, not inside one hospital
Controlled public transparency: the public reads the current plan and its authority, never rumour
Regional volunteers and assistance qualified before they are used
nose.solution: DRS beside Veoci: Veoci runs the incident inside the institution; DRS coordinates the region — leadership, capacity, the affected population — under one authority-controlled record.

evidence.experiment: Regional exercise with two or more facilities; time-stamp capacity requests and answers

evidence.claim: Public acknowledgement rate of plan changes rises and rumour-driven load falls
evidence.experiment: Measure acknowledgement rate and call-centre / diversion load, baseline vs pilot

evidence.claim: A regional buyer exists (health department, hospital association, county) who owns the cross-organization gap
evidence.experiment: Buyer validation interviews (S20 exit criterion: validated buyer)

nose.needs: Protect a known population in a bounded environment during safety, security, infrastructure or severe-weather disruption.
outcomes: Every person accounted for and every welfare need (heat, shelter, water, transport) recorded and fulfilled
Blankets, water, heat, transport and facility capacity allocated against the intake
Every relocation and plan change with its approver
nose.solution: DRS beside Sentinel: Sentinel notifies and checks; DRS fulfils — intake, allocation, provenance, polling, replay-to-drill, resource scenarios before the event.

evidence.claim: Time-to-account-for population and time-to-shelter fall vs the campus's current drill baseline
evidence.experiment: Two drills, one without and one with DRS, same scenario (winter freeze), timed

evidence.claim: Supplies reach recorded needs with fewer duplicate emergency labour hours
evidence.experiment: Count labour hours and duplicate deliveries per drill
Segment interviews rank the three axes

items: Responsive React interface (phone portrait, phone landscape, desktop landscape / full screen)

risks.issue: A false responder receives authority or resources
risks.mitigation: Verified roster with rank / authority; every grant is a named-human row; unauthorized requests refused and recorded

risks.issue: A recommendation is acted on as a decision
risks.mitigation: AI recommends and organizes; authorized humans retain command; no commit without a named human-authority event (R-CORE)

risks.risk: Privacy and sensitive data; healthcare compliance
risks.issue: Welfare and medical needs are personal data
risks.mitigation: Minimum intake; role-scoped visibility; compliance review before the healthcare pilot

risks.issue: The public reads rumour faster than the plan
risks.mitigation: Controlled public transparency: the current plan, its version and its authority are the public record
Coordinate across, never replace; MVP 1 needs no integration; ingestion lands in MVP 3

risks.issue: The event takes the network down
risks.mitigation: Offline-first record with replay on reconnect; the standalone-HTML discipline of the 2525 domain plays

risks.issue: Long cycles; reliance on the system in a life-safety context
risks.mitigation: Pilot through a partner customer first; the record is evidence, not a promise; scope of reliance written into the pilot agreement

crs.name: Verified authority + roster
crs.in: DRS-01.01.IN — a responder, official or volunteer is admitted only after verification by a named authority; rank / authority is on the record
crs.out: DRS-01.01.OUT — 100% of grants carry the verifier's identity and time; an unverified request is refused and recorded (target set after the baseline pilot)

crs.name: Needs intake
crs.in: DRS-02.01.IN — any affected person or field responder can submit a need (heat, shelter, water, transport, capacity) from a phone in ≤ 3 taps
crs.out: DRS-02.01.OUT — every need has a timestamp, a location, a priority and a state (open / assigned / fulfilled)

crs.name: Resource inventory + gap analysis
crs.in: DRS-03.01.IN — resources, facilities and supplies are listed with quantity, location, owner and qualification
crs.out: DRS-03.01.OUT — a live gap view: needs open vs resources available, per scenario

crs.name: Assignment + fulfilment
crs.in: DRS-04.01.IN — an authorized person assigns a resource to a need; the assignee acknowledges; fulfilment is confirmed by the need's owner
crs.out: DRS-04.01.OUT — need → assignment and assignment → fulfilment times recorded for 100% of needs

crs.name: Plan versioning + authority traceability
crs.in: DRS-05.01.IN — Plan v1 → Event → Change → Authority → Plan v2; every change names its authorizer
crs.out: DRS-05.01.OUT — the user reads what changed, why, who authorized it, what to do now; an unversioned change cannot exist

crs.name: Collective intelligence (eXeL polling)
crs.in: DRS-06.01.IN — concerns and priorities are collected from the workforce / public through eXeL polling sessions (33 languages, phone-first)
crs.out: DRS-06.01.OUT — themes (3/6/9) with summaries feed the plan revision; time from concern to revision recorded
crs.evidence: SOURCED (the eXeL AI Polling engine exists: Cubes 1–9)

crs.name: Controlled public transparency
crs.in: DRS-07.01.IN — the public / workforce reads the current plan, its version and its authority; nothing more
crs.out: DRS-07.01.OUT — acknowledgement rate of each revision measured

crs.name: Three resource plans
crs.in: DRS-08.01.IN — Conservative / Baseline / Aggressive plans with assumptions, cost, resources and the trigger for changing plans
crs.out: DRS-08.01.OUT — the plan in force and its trigger are visible at all times; a plan change is a versioned, authorized event

crs.name: Operational record + replay (R-CORE)
crs.in: DRS-09.01.IN — every mark, grant, assignment, change and refusal is one canonical row; the record replays
crs.out: DRS-09.01.OUT — replay reconstructs who knew what, who authorized what, what changed, what moved, what happened; replay hash stable
crs.evidence: SOURCED (R-CORE spec; the Drone-2525 domain play carries a working replay hash and register)

crs.name: Simulation + qualification
crs.in: DRS-10.01.IN — the three scenarios run against the record; readiness is measured
crs.out: DRS-10.01.OUT — simulation vs actual performance reported per event

crs.name: Cross-system ingestion
crs.in: DRS-11.01.IN — GridOS / Veoci / Sentinel / CrisisCommand facts and events enter the record with provenance; DRS never replaces them
crs.out: DRS-11.01.OUT — an ingested fact carries its source and time; conflicts are shown, not resolved silently

crs.name: Three interfaces
crs.in: DRS-12.01.IN — phone portrait, phone landscape, desktop landscape / full screen
crs.out: DRS-12.01.OUT — every workflow completes at 390 px wide and in landscape; gated in CI like the 2525 domain plays
crs.evidence: SOURCED (the 2525 harness runs both orientations in CI)

crs.name: Validation + evidence program
crs.in: DRS-13.01.IN — the thirteen S16 metrics are the columns of every pilot record
crs.out: DRS-13.01.OUT — WTP ranges and NBA deltas are written only from measured pilot columns
